ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 Amendment, adopted 26 April 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Registered Entities (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Market Entities Registration (State Council Order No. 746, effective 1 March 2022); Foreign Investment Security Review Measures (effective 18 January 2021).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the investing company's Certificate of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent registrar in the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path for Hague Convention member states, used exclusively: notarize the document in the country of origin, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority of that state. The People's Republic of China is a member of the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention effective 7 November 2023, so no Chinese consular legalization is added after the Apostille. Consular legalization path for non-member states, used exclusively and never sequentially with Apostille: notarize, then legalize through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the country of origin, then legalize through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that country.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active Status for the investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official corporate registry or registrar of companies in the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path for Hague Convention member states, used exclusively: notarize the certified certificate unitself, then affix a Hague Apostille from the competent authority of the issuing state. China recognizes the Apostille since 7 November 2023; do not add consular legalization. Consular legalization path for non-Hague states, used exclusively: notarize the certificate, then authenticate through the state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the issuing state. Never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the WFOE and designating the authorized signatory and agent for bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path for Hague Convention states, used exclusively: execute the resolution, notarize it in the source jurisdiction, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority. Because China acceded to the Apostille Convention on 7 November 2023, no consular legalization is required or permitted after the Apostille. For non-Hague states, use the exclusive consular legalization sequence: notarize, authenticate at the source state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the source state. Never combine both paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Articles of Association, constitutional documents, or by-laws of the investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary, registered office service provider, or corporate registrar of the investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention countries, the certified copy must be notarized in the state of origin and then issued with a Hague Apostille by the competent authority; this path is exclusive and sufficient for use in China since the Convention entered into force for China on 7 November 2023. For non-Apostille states, use only the consular legalization path: notarize, obtain authentication from the foreign ministry of the source state, and then obtain legalization from the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that state. Never add one path after the other.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the investing entity's principal bank confirming account conduct and standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investing entity's banker or relationship bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route for Hague Convention member states, used exclusively: issue the letter on bank letterhead, notarize the signature, then apply for a Hague Apostille from the competent authority. No Chinese consular legalization follows. Consular legalization route for non-member states, used exclusively: notarize the bank letter, authenticate through the source state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that state. The two authentication regimes are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of identity for each ultimate beneficial owner, director, legal representative, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the person's country of residence or the relevant consular authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille states, the identity pages must be notarized and then covered by a Hague Apostille from the state's competent authority; this is the exclusive path accepted for foreign public documents in China effective 7 November 2023. For non-Hague states, use only the consular legalization sequence: notarize the copy, have it authenticated by the source state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then legalize it at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that state. Never apply Apostille and consular legalization to the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, and their family members and close associates must be screened before engagement and continuously monitored against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, Interpol Red Notices, the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list, the PBOC anti-money-laundering watch lists, and the SAMR blacklist. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), including verification of source of wealth and source of funds through audited financial statements, tax returns, bank statements, and independent negative news checks. WFOE principals, transaction counterparties, and private-banking wire beneficiaries must be matched by full name, alias, date of birth, and nationality; any match or ambiguous hit triggers escalation to the compliance committee and, where required, a suspicious transaction report to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center. Re-screening must occur at least annually and immediately upon any ownership change, sanction designation, negative media event, or unusual transaction trigger. All screening evidence must be retained for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Independent Declaration System accessible through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be expressed in simplified Chinese characters. The mandatory four-tier name sequence is administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry or operational characteristic plus organizational form, which for a WFOE is Limited Liability Company or Limited Company in Chinese structural terms. English and pinyin transliterations are not registered by SAMR and may be used only for practical banking and contractual identification, provided they remain consistent with the registered Chinese name and do not create confusion. The English transliteration should be disclosed to the bank, tax authority, and foreign counterparties, but it carries no statutory registration effect.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When the name declaration is rejected, the applicant must first obtain the written rejection notice from the SAMR or its local market regulation bureau. A corrected name and supporting evidence, including trademark search results and a copy of the parent company registration certificate, should be submitted through the same online clearance portal. If the local authority confirms the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the market regulation authority at the next higher level or with the same-level people's government within 60 days of receiving the written decision, in accordance with the Administrative Reconsideration Law. If the reconsideration outcome is still adverse, the applicant may bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months of the reconsideration decision. Name reservations are valid for 30 days and extensions are not automatic; a written extension request must be filed before expiry and may be granted once for another 30 days at the discretion of the registration authority. If not extended, the applicant must re-file a fresh name declaration and recommence the clearance process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE engaging in single-family-office and private investment holding activities, a virtual office, commercial mailbox, or bare registered address is not permissible and will be rejected by the local SAMR, the tax authority, and the commercial bank. PRC company law requires an identifiable and usable domicile, and bank account onboarding requires proof of a physical lease, property ownership documentation or landlord consent, an entrance sign, and the actual presence of management or personnel. Virtual office arrangements are treated as evidence of shell-company risk and will trigger enhanced UBO disclosure, a likely refusal to issue VAT invoices, and a probable administrative penalty for falsely declaring the registered address. If an executive business center is used, it must be a licensed shared-office provider with a genuine service agreement, dedicated desk or meeting-room space, reception facilities, and the WFOE must maintain its books, records, corporate seals, and at least one responsible employee at that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: High, estimated 60 to 75 percent probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the municipal market regulation bureau or tax authority within the first 24 months for an SFO WFOE with no third-party revenue and minimal staffing. Checklist for readiness: i) a current lease agreement in the WFOE's name, stamped and aligned with the registered address; ii) visible signage matching the Chinese registered name; iii) utility bills, property management invoices, or sanitation receipts for the preceding six months; iv) at least one full-time employee with social insurance and payroll records tied to the registered address; v) annual tax filings, bank statements, and board minutes demonstrating real investment-management substance; vi) corporate records, share register, UBO declaration file, and executed investment agreements kept on the premises; vii) no more than ten other companies registered at the same address. Failure to satisfy these items may result in deregistration, a compliance blacklisting of the legal representative, or revocation of the tax registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official SAMR company name clearance and incorporation registration filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory official fee abolished; no government registration fee payable for enterprise incorporation in China.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fee for drafting WFOE Articles of Association, shareholders resolution, corporate governance charter, and incorporation application package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a foreign-invested company with investment-holding and family-office scope; billed at hourly rates or fixed fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the mandatory documentary bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities in the investor's home jurisdiction and Chinese Embassy or Consulate where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official notary fees, apostille fees, foreign-ministry authentication fees, and Chinese consular legalization tariffs as published by the respective authorities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of foreign incorporation documents, board resolutions, Articles of Association, bank reference letter, and passport copies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation agency and notary office in China
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-page certified translation market rate plus notarization of translation accuracy.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Secure registered physical office lease deposit and first quarterly rent in a permitted commercial or shared executive office center
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial lease market benchmark for a suitable office in a second-tier or third-tier Chinese city or a serviced-office contract in a first-tier city.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seals: company seal, legal representative seal, finance seal, and contract seal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local market fee for engraving and filing of four standardized seals with the public security filing system.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner information declaration filing with PBOC and SAMR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory filing fee; if outsourced to an agent, service fees apply separately.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registration, foreign exchange registration, social insurance registration, and corporate bank account opening assistance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed local service provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for compliance support with tax bureau, SAFE, social security authority, and commercial bank onboarding procedures.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance manual, PEP and sanctions screening procedure, and initial screening of all UBOs and counterparties
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance consulting partner or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a tailored single-family-office AML/CFT framework satisfying PBOC expectations and international bank requirements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Local counsel corporate and commercial substance opinion for the bank and tax authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee for a legal opinion confirming WFOE corporate validity, UBO transparency, and operational substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024), Articles 23-25, 26-36, 47 and 59-75; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 6 and 14; Regulation of the People's Republic of China on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746), Articles 8-17.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) acting through the local Market Supervision Administration / Government Service Center enterprise registration window at the municipality or province where the WFOE is domiciled.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company (with the integrated Foreign Investment Information Report) together with the notarized Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital is prescribed for a WFOE used as a passive Single Family Office holding vehicle. The sole shareholder must subscribe for the full registered capital in the Articles of Association, and under Article 47 of the Company Law all capital contributions must be paid in full within five years from incorporation unless a shorter period is required by administrative regulation. There is no blocked escrow-account requirement at state level; however, inbound foreign-currency capital contributions must be routed through a SAFE-registered capital account after foreign exchange registration is completed and cannot be made directly through ordinary settlement accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [●] WFOE LIMITED. Adopted by the first director or board in writing on the [●] day of [●], 20[●], at [●], People's Republic of China. WHEREAS the Company is a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company formed under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China for the purposes of private investment holding, single-family office treasury functions, and ancillary consulting; and WHEREAS the sole shareholder of the Company has lawfully subscribed to the entire registered capital of the Company; and WHEREAS it is necessary and desirable that the board adopt resolutions relating to the share capital subscription, designation of the registered office, approval of banking arrangements and appointment of statutory officers. NOW THEREFORE the board, acting by unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting, RESOLVES as follows: 1. Share Capital Subscription. The subscription by the sole shareholder of the entire registered capital of RMB [●] is ratified and confirmed. The board shall cause the registered capital to be paid in full within five years from the date of establishment or such later date as may be permitted by law, and shall execute all capital contribution schedules, confirmations, declarations and statutory filings necessary to evidence such payment. 2. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company shall be located at [●], being within the jurisdiction of the [●] Market Supervision Administration. The board approves the adoption of the lease agreement and directs the general manager to maintain the registered-address documentation in the statutory books and to notify the registrar of any future change. 3. Banking Authority. The board designates [●] Bank as the principal banker. The legal representative, together with one other authorized signatory, is authorized to open and maintain RMB basic deposit accounts, foreign currency capital accounts, custody accounts and securities accounts as appropriate, to execute banking mandates, to arrange wires, to sign loan or credit documents solely as authorized by subsequent resolutions, and to do all acts necessary to operate the treasury accounts of the Company. The bank may rely on this resolution until written revocation. 4. Statutory Officers. The board appoints [●] as executive director and legal representative, [●] as general manager, and [●] as supervisor. The supervisor shall not concurrently serve as legal representative, executive director, or general manager. All officers shall serve in accordance with the Articles of Association, and their duties, authorities and compensation shall be fixed in employment or appointment letters. 5. Authorized Executions. Each officer is hereby authorized to execute, submit, notarize and file all documents required to implement these resolutions, including tax registrations, bank forms, lease documents, foreign exchange filings, annual report filings and any regulatory applications. 6. Ratification. All acts taken prior to the date of this resolution by the promoters or the initial officers in connection with the incorporation and registration of the Company are ratified, confirmed and approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Negative List Screening and Enterprise Name Pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) via the China National Integrated Online Government Service Platform / National Enterprise Registration One-Stop Window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for pre-approval of the proposed Chinese legal name of the WFOE and simultaneously screen the proposed business scope against the current Negative List for Foreign Investment Access. If the scope covers passive private investment holding and family-office treasury management for high-net-worth clients, the sector is generally open; the applicant should not include regulated activities such as deposit-taking, securities brokerage, fund management, or trust business without separate financial licenses. The foreign investor must provide notarized and, where applicable, apostilled identification or corporate documents, and the submission must include a power of attorney naming a local contact person for service of documents. The system will issue a Name Pre-Approval Notice with a validity period.
required_dossiers: Notarized and apostilled corporate registration certificate or passport certificate of the foreign investor
Power of attorney appointing the local contact person
Identification document of the proposed legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name pre-approval is refused as conflictive or illegal, revise the proposed Chinese name and business scope and resubmit within 10 working days; the refusal notice must state the reason, and no adverse consequence attaches to the legal person unless the entity is already registered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment Filing, Articles of Association Submission and Business License Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration / Government Service Center One-Stop Enterprise Registration Window (SAMR).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name approval, execute the Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder, appoint the initial executive director, general manager, legal representative and supervisor, and complete the Establishment Registration Application. File the integrated Foreign Investment Information Report with SAMR under the Foreign Investment Law. Submit the registered-address certificate (lease plus property ownership certificate or landlord consent letter), capital contribution schedule, identity proofs, and appointment documents. SAMR reviews the filing; if compliant, it issues the Business License with the unified social credit code and the establishment registration notice. The entity becomes a legal person on the date of issuance. The Business License is the principal authorization to open bank accounts and obtain all post-registration approvals.
required_dossiers: Notarized and apostilled foreign investor identification and good standing evidence
Registered address lease contract and property ownership certificate or landlord consent
Appointment documents and identification of legal representative, directors, general manager, and supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query or rejection, cure the stated defect within 15 days; common cures include replacing an ineligible legal representative, correcting business scope wording to remove regulated financial services, or submitting missing landlord consent. A rejected filing may be amended and resubmitted without affecting the priority date under the Market Entity Registration Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Seals, Tax, Social Insurance and Statistical Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraving service points; State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; and the local statistics bureau, all accessed through the regional integrated government service platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one business day after receipt of the Business License, apply to a public security authorized engraving shop to produce the company seal, legal representative seal, finance seal, invoice seal and contract seal, in compliance with public security registration. Then complete tax qualification confirmation through the Electronic Tax Bureau to obtain the tax registration identity and handle invoice quota, issuance and monthly or quarterly tax filings. Register with social insurance and housing fund authorities, and complete statistical basic-unit reporting. For a WFOE, also ensure the integrated Foreign Investment Information Report was forwarded to the hierarchical information system. Use the unified social credit code in all filings.
required_dossiers: Seal Registration Application and Public Security Bureau approval record
Legal representative and general manager identification cards or passports
Social insurance and housing fund registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration or social insurance registration is suspended due to missing data, contact the relevant municipal call center and submit paper forms; no fine is imposed if the delay is cured within the statutory grace period, and the registration date is retroactively set using the Business License date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Formalization: First Board Resolution, Statutory Books and Officer Ratification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board and sole shareholder with local SAMR registration window for any officer change after license issuance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt the written resolution in lieu of a meeting, adopting the pro-forma resolution covering share capital subscription, registered office, bank appointments and officer appointments. Issue the share certificate or equity certificate to the sole shareholder. Open and maintain statutory corporate books: register of members, register of directors, supervisors and senior managers, meeting minutes and capital contribution ledger. Confirm that the legal representative, executive director, general manager and supervisor are not disqualified under the Company Law, for example through bankruptcy or enforcement blacklists. If the persons originally filed with SAMR have changed, submit a registration-change application; otherwise file the resolution with the statutory books for audit and banking use.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution in Chinese or bilingual formal text
Appointment letters and consents to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a statutory officer is challenged by SAMR, remove or replace the disqualified person by a new board resolution and file the amended appointment; the company should not sign bank or investment instruments until the corrected officer list is filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration and Capital Contribution Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank branch selected by the company, acting as SAFE agent, and ultimately the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); People's Bank of China RMB account registration system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a RMB basic deposit account at the selected bank and, if the shareholder will remit foreign currency as registered capital, open a foreign currency capital account through the bank's SAFE-agent channel. Submit the Foreign Investment Information Report and establishment registration documents to the bank; the bank enters the FDI registration into SAFE's system. After authorization, the shareholder may remit the subscribed capital into the capital account. Each withdrawal for operating expenses must comply with the capital account payment instructions and business transaction documentation. Within 30 days of each contribution, update the capital ledger and, if applicable, complete the annual report. This step completes the incorporator's funding obligation prescribed by the Company Law.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
SAFE Foreign Investment Basic Information Registration Form
Legal representative and authorized signatory identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE returns the registration for discrepancy, such as inconsistent beneficiary, investor name or investment scope, correct the applicable identification or expand the business scope first at SAMR and then resubmit to the same bank under a new application; remitted funds can be returned to the remitter in full if registration is not complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Licensing Exemption Assessment and Ongoing Regulatory Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Financial Regulatory Administration and China Securities Regulatory Commission only if regulated financial business is added later; for the passive SFO, no industrial licensing authority applies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the registered scope is ISIC 6430 passive private investment holding as a Single Family Office, confirm in writing through a legal opinion that the entity does not trigger any operating license, environmental impact assessment or industrial civil-defense permit. The company should maintain an internal compliance memorandum documenting that it will not conduct deposit-taking, trust, securities brokerage, fund-raising or commodity warehousing activities without the required authorization. If any regulated activity is later added, apply to the competent financial regulator for a separate license before commencing the activity. File the annual market entity annual report with SAMR by June 30, complete corporate income tax and any applicable value-added tax declarations, and update the Foreign Investment Information Report upon any material change.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local regulator or market authority questions the SFO's exemption, submit the legal opinion and Articles of Association to the relevant administration; if the authority still asserts regulation, file an application for the specific financial license or narrow the business scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation; the entity is an office-only passive holding vehicle.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory operating license for a passive SFO; regulated financial services, if added later, would require a separate license from the National Financial Regulatory Administration or the China Securities Regulatory Commission.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no EIA requirement for a non-physical SFO office environment; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the entity has no regulated discharge points, VOC emission sources, or hazardous waste generation; office waste management follows municipal solid waste rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as a manufacturing or warehousing permit. As an office-only tenant, the WFOE must obtain or confirm the landlord's building fire safety acceptance certificate, maintain basic fire extinguishers and emergency signage, and register the business office with local fire rescue authorities if required; no separate industrial Civil Defense fire license is triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, administered by provincial and municipal tax service bureaux; electronic compliance is transacted through the China Electronic Taxpayer (e-Taxation) platform operated by STA and its regional portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: After incorporation, the WFOE receives an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); this USCC is the statutory tax identification number for all PRC resident legal persons. Step 2: Within 30 days of obtaining the business license, the company must complete tax registration on the China Electronic Taxpayer platform by filing entity information, registered address, legal representative, registered capital, bank account details, accounting system, and intended tax types. Step 3: The local competent tax authority confirms registration and assigns tax type statuses for Corporate Income Tax (CIT), Value-Added Tax (VAT), stamp duty, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, and Individual Income Tax withholding for employees. Step 4: For a foreign non-resident enterprise that has not created a WFOE but derives PRC-source income, the non-resident enterprise obtains a non-resident tax identification number from the competent SAT office or through a qualified PRC withholding agent using the same electronic taxpayer platform; the application must include legal existence evidence, foreign tax residence certificate, contract or income source documents, and completed non-resident tax registration forms in the STA system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not maintain a check-the-box or equivalent entity classification election. A WFOE is automatically a PRC tax resident enterprise and is taxable at entity level on its worldwide income; no pass-through or transparent election is available for a Chinese limited liability company. Hybrid mismatch elections are not part of the PRC domestic law framework; any perceived hybrid outcomes are addressed by the general anti-abuse rule, transfer pricing rules, and controlled foreign corporation rules during audit.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual VAT taxable sales is the statutory threshold for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration. A foreign-invested WFOE must complete tax registration regardless of turnover, but below this threshold it may remain a small-scale taxpayer. The WFOE's family office and investment management services, where taxable, generally fall under the VAT category of modern services at 6%; the 13% standard headline rate applies to sales of goods. Passive investment holding and dividend or interest income do not attract VAT until separately charged as a management fee.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: PRC VAT invoices are governed by the STA Golden Tax Phase IV system and the nationwide fully digitalized electronic invoice framework. All VAT special invoices must be issued through the STA-approved invoice management system or the China Electronic Taxpayer platform. Each e-invoice carries a unique invoice code and digital anti-counterfeit signature; issuance data is transmitted to SAT and cross-matched with VAT returns, Customs declarations, and bank foreign-exchange data. There is no physical tax-office pre-clearance stamp for each invoice, but the system blocks issuance to non-qualified sellers, applies the correct tax classification code, and suspends input tax credits on abnormal or unmatched invoices until verification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: PRC VAT general taxpayers may claim the 0% export VAT rate only when goods are properly declared to Customs and physically exported from PRC customs territory, or when a supply is a cross-border taxable service or intangible asset designated under the VAT zero-rating rules and supplied to a non-resident recipient with the service wholly consumed outside the PRC. For a WFOE single family office, passive family asset custody and private investment holding are not automatically zero-rated; the tax authority must confirm eligibility for any designated offshore service with a written qualification determination, supported by a cross-border service contract, invoice, bank foreign-exchange receipt, and proof that the overseas family or entity is the beneficial consumer outside China.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Goods Declaration (Export Customs Declaration Form) bearing an accepted export declaration number; the Indian-style 'Bill of Entry' designation is not a PRC statutory document name.
Ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or rail/road multimodal transport document evidencing actual physical exit from the PRC customs territory.
Commercial export invoice, packing list, and signed export sales contract reflecting the overseas buyer and agreed payment terms.

Bank foreign-exchange receipt or SAFE-designated bank export proceeds collection confirmation; in PRC practice the 'Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC)' nomenclature is not used, and the required evidence is the bank-issued inward foreign exchange income declaration or cross-border RMB settlement receipt.

For cross-border services, the cross-border service agreement, service export invoice, and Trade in Services Foreign Exchange Income and Expense Declaration filed through the SAFE reporting channel, together with any SAT approval notice confirming zero-rating eligibility.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, General Administration of Customs, and SAFE perform automated tripartite data matching for every export zero-rating claim. If the export proceeds are not received or waived through an approved exemption within the 180-day foreign-exchange collection period, the claiming enterprise is recharacterized as making a domestic taxable sale; the previously refunded VAT and input credits are clawed back, the applicable VAT plus urban maintenance and construction tax and education surcharges must be paid, and late payment surcharge accrues at 0.05% per day. Where export refund fraud is established under Article 66 of the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law, the tax authority recovers the fraudulently obtained refund and imposes a fine of one to five times the amount, and may suspend the enterprise's export refund processing. If the amount crosses criminal thresholds, the responsible individuals may face criminal liability under Article 204 of the Criminal Law, with escalating imprisonment and fines or asset confiscation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese yuan (RMB) is not freely convertible on the capital account, while current account transactions for trade in goods and services are generally convertible under SAFE verification. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment (FDI), external borrowings, and outbound investments, require prior regulatory approval, registration, or filing with SAFE. A WFOE engaged in single-family office investment holding must secure an FDI registration certificate and a SAFE registration for its capital account. Profit remittances are permitted for genuine historical earnings provided the enterprise has completed annual compliance filings, audited financial statements, tax clearance, and verified the source of the distributable profits. Dividends can be remitted abroad in RMB-converted foreign currency, but each remittance requires supporting documentation including board resolutions, interim audit reports, and tax payment proof. Capital injection funds must be lodged in a designated capital escrow account (FDI settlement account), and the use of these funds is strictly limited to the approved business scope and cannot be transferred into onshore securities markets without special clearance. The corporation must demonstrate legitimate investor identities, transparent upstream funding sources, and adherence to the negative list for foreign investment. Since this entity is in a restricted category of private investment holding, it is not eligible for automatic current account convertibility and must maintain a robust, audit-verified trail of each cross-border flow to satisfy both PBOC and SAFE requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated into China through designated foreign currency accounts or domestic settlement accounts within a monitoring period generally aligned with the standard 180-day trade settlement cycle. For current account receipts, the enterprise has the option to retain the foreign currency in an offshore or onshore foreign exchange settlement account, but all inflows must be reported under the SAFE trade monitoring system. Since 2012, mandatory surrender obligations have been abolished, but the enterprise must complete a bank-assisted receipt verification process, and any excess holding beyond normal operational needs may trigger SAFE inquiry. For the WFOE single family office, if export operations are not the core business, the actual trading activities will be zero, said rule applies only to export-heavy subsidiary operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability with legal constraints. Foreign fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not licensed to open domestic bank accounts or provide deposit-taking services for entities in mainland China. Non-bank payment institutions must hold a local payment business permit, which is granted only to qualified Chinese companies, and they cannot operate as a full-scale commercial bank. For cross-border settlements, a WFOE must rely on domestic tier-1 banks for all RMB and FX clearing. Offshore EMIs can only act as ancillary prepaid tool providers for certain employee expense scenarios, not as the primary treasury clearing rail. Any attempt to route capital injections or profit dividends through an EMI will be rejected by SAFE and may trigger anti-money laundering sanctions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and ultimate beneficial owner(s) are required to appear physically at the bank branch for a face-to-face KYC interview during the account opening process. Remote or consular proxy opening is not permitted for a WFOE without an established physical presence in mainland China. At least one authorized signatory who is a Chinese-resident director or a senior manager with a valid employment contract must attend in person. The bank will conduct an interview covering the origin of funds, expected transaction volume, counterparty structure, and source of wealth. If a director is non-resident and cannot be physically present, a notarized power of attorney and a consular-legalized documentary package may allow a local finance officer to complete the interview, but the final approval must be granted by the bank's compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity for a single-family office with multi-jurisdictional asset holding layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete corporate org chart from the WFOE up to the ultimate individual beneficiaries, including certified certificates of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, shareholder registers, register of directors, and notarized identity documents of all natural persons holding 10% or more equity or effective control. Provide third-party legal opinion from a reputable international law firm confirming the chain of ownership and absence of anonymous shell entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth and source of funds for high-net-worth family assets to be injected as FDI capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements from the originating family trust or holding vehicle for the past three years, bank statements showing the historical accumulation of funds, sale agreements or inheritance certificates for any major asset sales, tax payment receipts, and a professionally prepared source-of-wealth report. All documents must be certified by a CPA and, if sourced from a foreign jurisdiction, legalized or apostilled and translated into Chinese by a sworn translator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or politically exposed person (PEP) linkage associated with the family office founder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full adverse media search report from a recognized investigation vendor (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv) covering at least a five-year lookback period, an enhanced PEP screening report, a written explanation letter from the client addressing any hits, and, if applicable, evidence of termination of any questionable business relationships. For any residual PEP risk, a board resolution appointing a designated local AML compliance officer and implementing enhanced transaction monitoring will be required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purpose and intended usage of the capital account funds, given the ISIC 6430 status as a private investment holding and potential gap between declared scope and actual securities custody activities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A granular three-year business plan with projected capital deployment schedule, a legal memorandum from a Chinese licensed law firm confirming compliance with the FDI negative list, a copy of the Ministry of Commerce or local MOC filing, and written undertakings that no investor funds will be used for prohibited equity trading or securities margin activity. The bank will require a separate undertaking to maintain all securities custody assets through qualified custodians and to update SAFE on any change of business purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: FDI capital injection must be routed from the overseas parent or family trust bank account via international SWIFT MT103 payment into the WFOE's designated capital escrow account opened with a tier-1 Chinese bank. The remitter must exactly identify the WFOE and the SAFE FDI registration number, and the payment purpose code must be 'Investment - New Paid-in Capital' (code typically 91001). The bank will perform a capital verification and coordinate with the local Administration for Market Regulation to ensure the capital is registered. All foreign currency received in the capital account must be converted to RMB through the designated bank's FX system, with a capital application form submitted to SAFE and monitored against the approved capital amount. If the injection includes intellectual property or other non-cash assets, an asset appraisal report from a licensed Chinese appraiser and a supplementary verification through SAFE are mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Approved operational trade settlements should be executed using SWIFT MT103 messages for supplier payments under a verified commercial invoice and import customs declaration. For larger and riskier transactions, the WFOE may open an import Letter of Credit (L/C) with its tier-1 bank, providing standardized terms including INCOTERMS and required transport documents. Documentary collections are acceptable where the counterparty risk is low and the underlying trade contract is clearly documented. All outbound payments need a tax declaration confirmation from the local tax bureau, and for service imports, the relevant tax registration certificate must be shown to prevent money laundering. For family office external management and professional fees, payments must be routed through the basic operational account with careful purpose descriptions consistent with the approved business license.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts (FX forwards) with domestic authorized banks to hedge actual trade or investment exposure. These must be linked to a genuine underlying transaction approved by SAFE.

Foreign currency swap agreements (FX swaps) for managing liquidity mismatches between RMB and foreign currency positions, strictly for trade financing or capital account settlement needs, subject to SAFE documentation.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) are permissible only for hedging medium-term foreign currency loan exposures and must have a maturity-matched debt service obligation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally prohibited onshore for Chinese entities, so treasury operations should not execute NDF contracts; any hedging of RMB must be done via deliverable forwards at a locally licensed bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Information Report / Annual Return to the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the local Administration for Market Regulation at the WFOE's registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the immediately preceding calendar year; first report for an entity established before 31 December is due no later than 30 June of the succeeding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the report is not filed by 30 June, the company is placed on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Credit Status and publicized; continued non-rectification for 3 years leads to inclusion on the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, with restrictions on government procurement, financing, tax incentives, customs clearance and secured transfers; under PRC Company Law, an enterprise that remains non-operational or fails to remedy the abnormal listing may ultimately face administrative revocation of its business license by SAMR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Information Report for Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; local commerce department for direct foreign investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the preceding calendar year, matching the SAMR annual report window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit, or submission of incomplete or false information, triggers a rectification order under Article 37 of the PRC Foreign Investment Law; refusal to correct may lead to a fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000, approximately USD 14,000 to USD 70,000, plus inclusion in the abnormal credit list and restrictions on subsequent cross-border capital and corporate change filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return and Final Settlement with audited financial statement support
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) via the local tax service bureau having jurisdiction over the WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return and final settlement for each calendar year must be filed no later than 31 May of the following year; quarterly provisional returns are due within 15 days after the close of each quarter; loss carry-forwards and annual deductions are determined in this final settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax from the day after the deadline; failure to file on time may incur a fine up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases; false declarations may attract an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax and potential criminal liability; the tax authority may apply enforced collection against bank deposits and other assets, but tax delinquency alone does not directly cause administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements presented to shareholders and retained for regulatory inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No standing public filing for a private WFOE; audited report is prepared for the shareholders' annual meeting and must be produced on demand to SAMR, STA, SAFE, MOFCOM and PBOC during audits and investigations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements must be completed and submitted to the shareholders' meeting before the annual meeting or approval decision; best practice and regulatory expectation is no later than 31 March for accelerated procedures or 31 May with the annual corporate income tax settlement, covering the calendar-year financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain the statutory independent audit is contrary to PRC Company Law and may cause annual report and tax settlements to be treated as non-genuine and non-compliant; sanctions include denial of tax deductions, abnormal credit listing, administrative fines for inaccurate disclosure, and enforcement actions against directors and supervisors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under PRC Company Law, statutory audit is absolute for every limited liability company, including a WFOE; there is no qualifying balance-sheet, turnover or headcount exemption. The audit duty applies even where an entity qualifies as a small or micro enterprise under Chinese SME statistical classification, such as fewer than 20 employees and annual revenue below RMB 10 million in service industries or comparable small-asset thresholds. For a single-family-office holding vehicle, the independent certified public accountant must audit assets, investments, liabilities, related-party balances and going concern; bank custody, securities and private investment holding activities further increase audit scope under PBOC and securities regulatory expectations. Public-interest and listing thresholds under CSRC rules do not apply unless the WFOE becomes listed or a licensed financial institution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Enterprise Accounting Standards (CAS / ASBE), which are IFRS-converged; eligible very small profit-making enterprises may apply the Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises (MSEAS) only when they are not financial or investment holding entities. A single-family-office investment holding WFOE is normally required to apply CAS with IFRS-based recognition and measurement principles for financial assets, impairment, revenue and disclosure.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must include the ultimate investor, actual controller and beneficial ownership chain in the annual foreign investment information report filed by 30 June with MOFCOM and SAMR. On any shareholding transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership, the company must apply for amendment of its SAMR registration within 30 days of the board or shareholder resolution and update the foreign investment information report within 30 days of the ownership change. There is no separate annual UBO certificate filing, but false or incomplete UBO disclosure is treated as false annual report information and exposes the company to correction orders and fines of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000, approximately USD 14,000 to USD 70,000.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 to USD 2,500 per annum in Tier-1 Chinese cities such as Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen and Guangzhou for a licensed registered-address, compliance correspondence and annual-filing agent; USD 400 to USD 1,200 in smaller cities; actual physical office lease is additional.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 to USD 10,000 for a standalone WFOE holding simple investment assets; USD 8,000 to USD 25,000 for multi-entity or consolidated single-family-office group audits; complex private equity, fund or holding arrangements may exceed USD 30,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard 25% CIT. No sector-specific incentive applies to a Single Family Office; however, the Small and Low-Profit Enterprise regime may grant effective rates as low as 5% if annual taxable income does not exceed RMB 3 million, employee count and total assets thresholds are met. Passive holding companies are generally excluded from preferential treatment unless substantive operational substance is demonstrated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual CIT Return Form A100000 (National Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, Category A) plus supporting schedules; filed through the State Taxation Administration's e-Tax Bureau portal. Quarterly provisional returns are filed through Form A200000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional filing and prepayment)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly returns due within 15 days after each quarter-end; annual reconciliation return due within 5 months after the calendar year-end (i.e., by May 31 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue - total revenue from core and incidental business activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE family office, report management fees, investment advisory fees, and any service income only where substantive services are rendered. Recompute income at fair market value on all cross-border related-party transactions; adjust for transfer pricing differences before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating cost - costs directly attributable to earning operating revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate common costs using consistent, auditable keys. Disallow expenses paid to foreign head office unless supported by arm's-length agreements and Chinese-valid vouchers; ensure that intra-group service charges meet the benefit test.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges, selling expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate management fees charged by foreign parent or sibling entities; disallow head-office general administrative expenses that are not rendered as specific services. For financial expenses, cap interest deductions at the statutory debt-equity ratio and benchmark interest rate under CIT implementation rules.

Dividends from Chinese resident companies are exempt from CIT on the receiving side. Dividends from foreign subsidiaries must be included in taxable income before claiming any foreign tax credit. Recharacterise loan or equity investments if thin capitalization rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income, reduced-income items, and other adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only interest on on-lending state treasury bonds or qualifying infrastructure funds qualify for exemption. Do not treat gains from indirect equity transfers of Chinese property as tax-exempt; such transactions may trigger outbound capital gains tax under Notice 698 and Article 120 of the CIT Implementation Regulations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions and loss carryover
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 5-year loss carryforward strictly. Family office losses from passive investment holding may be challenged if no business substance; reinstatement of loss utilization requires contemporaneous economic-substance documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate and computed CIT liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Standard rate 25%. If the WFOE qualifies as a small and low-profit enterprise, Schedule A107040 will apply differential rates. Foreign tax credit for taxes paid on foreign-sourced income must be claimed on Schedule A108000, capped at China's tax on that foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax on base-eroding payments to non-residents (e.g., interest, royalties, deemed dividends)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When the annual return reflects pre-withholding payments, a separate withholding declaration is required. Cite the relevant treaty article claimed and attach a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership statement. Failure to file contemporaneous supporting documents exposes the WFOE to late withholding penalties at 0.05% per day plus 50%-100% of under-withheld tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late returns: RMB 2,000 (one-off) plus RMB 50 for each additional month of delay, up to RMB 10,000. Late payment surcharge: 0.05% per day on the unpaid tax. Intentional non-filing with tax understated: a fine of 50% - 500% of the underpaid tax, plus criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the Criminal Law if the amount evaded exceeds RMB 100,000 and is above 10% of taxable income.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA rate, the foreign shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its resident jurisdiction, submit a treaty relief application form (together with the withholding tax return) to the Chinese in-charge tax bureau, provide evidence of beneficial ownership (i.e., no conduit arrangements, substantive business activity, no contractual obligation to pass on the dividend), and, where required, obtain an advance clearance or filing of the DTA application before the dividend distribution. Approval is generally completed within 10 working days. If the beneficial owner is a company, a minimum shareholding period of 365 days must be met; for interest, a similar ownership test applies only to related-party claims.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 10%; DTA reduction typically to 5-10% depending on the treaty and beneficial ownership (e.g., China-Luxembourg treaty provides 0% on interest in some conditions, but standard is 10%). Royalties: statutory 10%; DTA rate usually 7-10% (e.g., China-Hong Kong arrangement: 7% for royalties, 5% for interest if absolute beneficial owner). For all payments, a WHT is applied at payment source; a TRC and supporting documentation must be submitted to avoid audit adjustments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (contemporaneous documentation) is mandatory when the aggregate value of related-party transactions in one of the following categories exceeds: (a) tangible asset transfers (excluding within-China transactions) RMB 200 million; (b) intangible asset transfers RMB 100 million; (c) financial asset transfers RMB 100 million; (d) any other related-party transactions RMB 40 million. Master File is required when the group's consolidated turnover exceeds RMB 5 billion and the group begins cross-border related-party transactions within China.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although China does not have an Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime analogous to the UAE, general anti-avoidance rules under Article 47 of the CIT Law and Article 120 of the Implementation Regulations apply. Transactions lacking commercial substance and with core income-generating activities (CIGA) located outside China may be recharacterised. A Chinese WFOE holding passive family assets must demonstrate real management and decision-making in China (board meetings, office premises, local employees) to preserve its tax domicile and avoid being treated as a shell conduit subject to 10% WHT on outbound payments under the anti-abuse doctrine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting investment income, inflating management fees charged by the foreign parent, or fabricating non-existent loss carry-overs using sham intercompany contracts, thereby reducing taxable income below the actual level.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law (PRC): penalty of 50% up to 500% of the underpaid tax. Article 201 of the Criminal Law: fines and imprisonment of up to 7 years where the amount evaded exceeds RMB 100,000 or constitutes more than 10% of the tax payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil: court-ordered restitution of the evaded tax and penalties, personal asset freezing/attachment, and inclusion in the State Taxation Administration's blacklist triggering a high-level travel ban (exit restriction). Criminal: the legal representative and accountant in charge may be personally prosecuted with up to 7 years imprisonment for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping / Conduit Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE has no staff, no office, no actual investment decision-making, and serves purely as a conduit to route dividends or royalties to a tax-haven parent to obtain treaty benefits that would otherwise be denied; failing economic substance and beneficial ownership tests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 47 CIT Law (GAAR) and Article 120 Implementation Regulations: tax authority may recharacterise the payment and disallow treaty relief. Retrospective re-collection of 10% WHT on all outbound payments, plus interest at the lending benchmark rate; additional penalty up to 50% of the re-collected tax under Article 63 (penalty for underpayment).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil: directors who knowingly implemented the conduit arrangement are jointly and severally liable for the additional tax and penalties. Travel restriction (clearance to depart) will be imposed until the outstanding tax is settled. Criminal: if the recharacterisation leads to a determined underpayment exceeding RMB 100,000, directors may be prosecuted for tax evasion under Article 201 with up to 7 years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Undisclosed Offshore Accounts and Unreported Foreign Assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The family office uses hidden bank accounts outside China, transfers assets through shell companies in tax havens, and fails to report foreign-sourced income or foreign financial assets, breaching China's CRS obligations and foreign exchange control rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 10 of the Anti-Money Laundering Law (PRC): penalties of RMB 2 million - 10 million for institutions and up to RMB 1 million for liable individuals; confiscation of illegal gains. Foreign exchange control violations under SAFE Regulations attract fines of up to 30% of illegal FX transactions. For tax laundering, Article 191 of the Criminal Law applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil: all concealed assets are restituted, bank accounts frozen, and the company and directors are blacklisted across the tax and banking systems; travel ban issued under the Exit-Entry Administration Law. Criminal: directors may receive 5-10 years imprisonment for money laundering or 3-7 years for evasion of foreign-exchange controls, plus personal fines equal to twice the amount laundered.
